explanations: There is none. Liveness only reports that the process can serve HTTP, so a ClickHouse or Kafka outage does not cause restarts. Readiness runs dependency checks with a per-check timeout that aborts the underlying call and always clears its timer; results are cached for cacheMs and concurrent probes share one in-flight run, so probes cannot pile load onto dependencies. Only critical failures return 503, a failed geoip cache reports 'degraded' with 200, and SIGTERM flips readiness to 503 so traffic drains before shutdown.

geoip_cache has critical: false, so criticalDown is false (200) and degraded is true, giving status 'degraded'. runCheck catches errors into a 'fail' result, so nothing throws to produce a 500, and 'ok' requires no failures.

The first call sets this.inflight; the others see it non-null and return the same promise. After it settles the results are cached for cacheMs. The cache is empty initially, so pinging does happen, just once.

runCheck races the ping against a timer that aborts the controller and rejects after timeoutMs, producing a 'fail' result; clickhouse is critical so readiness returns 503. Liveness does not look at dependencies, so it keeps returning 200.
